scoring_inputs.source: CHIRPS (ClimateSERV) rain vs crop water demand

insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 879 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Fields are greenest in October, barest in March
insights.body: Satellite greenness of the farmland here peaks at 0.62 and drops to 0.41 (0 = bare, 1 = dense crop). The low months are when soil is most exposed to rain and wind.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rice, Salt-tolerant rice and Soybean score highest on climate, water and soil fit.
insights.source: Sowcast crop-fit score using measured climate and soil

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: +0.6 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 27.6 °C to about 28.2 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
